title: A projection operator approach for ultracold bosons coupled to a cavity
authors: Sarbarish Sen, Bimalendu Deb, K. Sengupta
abstract: We employ a projection operator technique to study the equilibrium phases and the non-equilibrium quench and ramp dynamics of ultracold bosons described by a two-dimensional (2D) Bose-Hubbard model coupled to a high-finesse cavity with competing local short-range and cavity-mediated long-range interactions. Our analysis relies on a systematic elimination of high-energy virtual hopping processes; this enables us to capture the effects of short-range quantum fluctuations on the phase diagram of the model while treating the cavity-induced long-range interaction within mean-field theory. We find that the phase boundaries between the superfluid (SF), supersolid (SS), charge-density-wave (CDW) and Mott insulating (MI) phases are significantly modified by the presence of these fluctuations. We use this approach to study the dynamics of bosons following a quench/ramp from the CDW to the SS and SF phases; our analysis indicates the presence of oscillatory dynamics characterized by a single frequency due to a quench which takes the system near the critical point. In contrast, for a quench deep inside the SF phase, the dynamics involves multiple frequencies. An explicit comparison with Gutzwiller mean-field theory shows the importance of quantum fluctuations in shaping such post-quench dynamics; this feature may be tested experimentally as we discuss. We also study the ramp dynamics of these bosons and identify a bound on the ramp rate above which the present method is expected to produce accurate results.
summary: This paper analyzes ultracold bosons in a cavity-coupled Bose-Hubbard model using a projection operator technique to account for quantum fluctuations. The study maps out the phase diagram and simulates quench dynamics, demonstrating that quantum fluctuations significantly alter phase boundaries and introduce characteristic single-frequency oscillations near quantum critical points compared to mean-field predictions.
main_problem: The study investigates the equilibrium phases and non-equilibrium dynamics of ultracold bosons coupled to a cavity, specifically focusing on the role of short-range quantum fluctuations.
main_result: Quantum fluctuations significantly modify the phase boundaries between SF, SS, CDW, and MI phases, and the dynamics near the critical point exhibit single-frequency oscillations distinct from mean-field predictions.
method: The authors employ a projection operator technique, which systematically eliminates high-energy virtual hopping processes, combined with mean-field theory for the long-range cavity interaction.
model_or_system: The system is modeled by ultracold bosons in a two-dimensional (2D) Bose-Hubbard model coupled to a high-finesse cavity, resulting in an extended Bose-Hubbard model.
key_observables: Superfluid (SF), Supersolid (SS), Charge-Density-Wave (CDW), and Mott Insulating (MI) phases; time evolution of superfluid order parameters and characteristic oscillation frequencies.
important_parameters: Hopping amplitude (J), on-site repulsion (U), cavity-mediated interaction strength (V), and quench/ramp rates.
main_assumptions: The method captures only short-range quantum fluctuations over mean-field theory and does not capture Kibble-Zurek scaling during ramps across critical points.
figures_summary: Figures compare the time evolution of the order parameter $|\Delta_A(t)|$ for quenches near the critical point (showing single-frequency oscillations) versus deep in the SF regime (showing multi-frequency dynamics), contrasting the projection operator method with mean-field theory.
paper_structure: The paper introduces the Hamiltonian and the atomic limit, develops the theoretical framework using the projection operator formalism for the ground state phase diagram, and finally analyzes non-equilibrium dynamics via quench and ramp simulations.
why_interesting: This work is highly relevant as it tackles the complex interplay between quantum fluctuations, long-range interactions, and non-equilibrium dynamics in systems relevant to quantum simulation using ultracold atoms in optical lattices.

For V/U ≤1/2, one finds translationally invariant MI phases with nA = nB (red) separated by partially polarized CDW phase with nA−nB = 1 sandwiched between them (light blue). For V/U > 0.5, one finds several fully polarized CDW phases with nB = 0 (dark blue); for these phases δn incoreses with µ/U as shown. The white region indicates instability of the system due to large V/U; see text for details.
